headline: Highest risk is medium: MinerU’s MCP/API surfaces can amplify Botpress outputs into prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors, but Botpress has no documented shared channel or write path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes an MCP Server and API surfaces, while Botpress is a chatbot agent that can emit content consumed elsewhere. A shared channel is plausible, but no direct bridge or provenance tracking is documented, so I cannot call it low. Uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than none.
conditions: IF Botpress outputs are routed into MinerU via MCP, API, or copied files
IF MinerU treats extracted text as instructions rather than inert content
mitigations: Disable any Botpress-to-MinerU automation path
Require provenance labels on all Botpress-generated text
Strip instructions from imported documents before MinerU processing
Use a manual review step before MinerU acts on Botpress output

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU processes local PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR text, and Botpress is a customer-support agent that may handle user content. Even though Botpress has network egress none, MinerU’s API/MCP surfaces create a plausible shared-workspace leakage path. The pair lacks documented isolation, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or file drop
IF sensitive documents are passed from Botpress into MinerU for extraction
mitigations: Separate Botpress and MinerU workspaces
Restrict MinerU inputs to non-sensitive test files
Turn off any automatic file forwarding from Botpress
Review logs for document contents after each run

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Botpress can install packages, while MinerU cannot write files, modify git, or execute shells. Their write-capability overlap is not documented, and MinerU’s self-isolation plus lack of write permissions makes direct conflict unlikely. The remaining risk is limited to unusual orchestration, so low fits.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF Botpress package installation mutates a shared runtime used by MinerU
mitigations: Run the agents in separate containers
Mount MinerU inputs read-only
Pin Botpress dependencies before shared runs
Avoid shared git worktrees or mutable caches

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU’s document-processing output can be treated as authoritative downstream, and Botpress is positioned to generate or relay content that MinerU may ingest. There is no documented verification layer between them, so A-to-B error propagation is plausible in default workflows. I choose medium because the pair can amplify mistakes even without explicit action authority.
conditions: IF MinerU output is used by Botpress without human verification
IF Botpress-generated text is converted into documents for MinerU to parse
mitigations: Add a human verification step before downstream use
Require source-document citations in MinerU outputs
Compare extracted fields against originals for a sample set
Block automatic action-taking from MinerU results

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no stated PHI, residency, or retention commitments. Botpress touches customer-support content and MinerU processes documents, but the profiles do not show a concrete compliance mismatch. Because the evidence is sparse, I keep this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through either agent
IF deployment policies impose retention or residency constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Disable regulated-data workflows until policies are confirmed
Document retention settings for both systems
Obtain a DPA or equivalent before production use
